releases.title: MFour Expands Digital Ad Exposure Intelligence to ChatGPT and Audio Streaming Platforms
releases.body:
MFour's OmniTraffic® Digital Ads feed now captures ad exposure across ChatGPT, social, video and audio apps, and connects it to each panelist's downstream behavior for attribution.

IRVINE, Calif., Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MFour Data Research today announced the launch of OmniTraffic® Digital Ads, expanding its digital ad exposure capabilities beyond social media to include AI, streaming video and audio platforms. The feed now captures advertising exposure across ChatGPT, YouTube, Spotify, Pandora and SoundCloud, alongside Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and X.

MFour's OmniTraffic® Digital Ads feed gives brands a unified view of advertising exposure across channels that increasingly shape the consumer journey. Because each exposure is tied to the same opted-in MFour consumer identity used across the company's behavioral data, researchers can connect media exposure with downstream actions including app usage, web activity, store visits, AI conversations, and purchases.

"Advertising is happening across more digital environments than ever, but measurement is still fragmented," said Chris St. Hilaire, Founder and CEO of MFour Data Research. "By connecting ad exposure across social platforms, streaming media, and AI to what those same consumers do next, we're giving brands a clearer view of the full journey and a stronger understanding of what happens after exposure."

Unlike modeled or inferred impressions, OmniTraffic® Digital Ads captures real, observed ad exposure from consenting, compensated consumers in MFour's first-party panel. Available fields vary by platform and can include advertiser information, promotion type, creative metadata, exposure timing and duration.

At launch, the feed includes approximately 60,000 consumers and 63 million ad exposures from the most recent 30-day period. For brand and insights teams, that expanded coverage creates new opportunities to evaluate advertising and brand lift across a broader mix of digital environments.

Learn more at MFour.com.

About MFour Data Research

MFour Data Research, founded in 2011, provides validated, opt-in consumer behavior and survey data powered by its Surveys On The Go® app and Fair Trade Data® model. The company's 13M+ consumer panel generates nine deterministic data streams — ChatGPT conversations, location, app usage, web browsing, receipts, demographics, attitudes, survey responses and behavior-triggered surveys — all connected to a single identity.

Through MFour Studio™, organizations can access these behavioral and survey signals to understand consumer journeys and measure outcomes, with DANI™ (Data Analytics Navigation Instructor), MFour's AI assistant, providing on-demand analysis across 4 billion monthly buyer signals. MFour is trusted by Samsung, Google, Amazon Ads, Microsoft, Hulu, Keurig Dr Pepper, Papa Johns and hundreds of other global brands.

Full Journey Intelligence. Know What to Do Next.

releases.title: Local Media Consortium Launches AI Accelerator
releases.body:
New program will help local media companies assess AI readiness, identify opportunities for implementation, and shape future training, resources and services

NEW YORK, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Local Media Consortium (LMC) today announced the launch of the AI Accelerator, a new program designed to help local media companies better understand, evaluate and implement artificial intelligence strategies that improve operations, strengthen business performance and support long-term sustainability. As part of the program, the LMC is partnering with Stellis AI to conduct an AI Readiness & Digital Tech Stack Assessment for participating members.

The assessment comes as artificial intelligence continues to move up the priority list for local media organizations. In the LMC's recent industry survey, 46% of respondents identified AI for operations as one of the top trends on their radar for 2026, underscoring growing interest in practical applications that can improve efficiency, streamline workflows and support business growth.

The AI Readiness & Digital Tech Stack Assessment will provide participating organizations with a comprehensive evaluation of their current technology environment, AI readiness, operational priorities and opportunities for implementation. Findings, which will be gleaned from a survey that kicked off on August 25, will help organizations identify practical ways to improve workflows, increase efficiency, reduce costs, strengthen audience engagement and uncover new revenue opportunities.

"Artificial intelligence has quickly moved from a future consideration to an active business priority for many local media organizations," said Fran Wills, CEO of the Local Media Consortium. "Our members are looking for practical guidance on where AI can create the greatest impact for their organizations. The AI Accelerator will help participants assess their readiness, identify opportunities and build a roadmap for implementation so they can make informed decisions with confidence."

Participating organizations will receive individualized findings and recommendations to support future planning and implementation efforts. Assessment results will remain proprietary to participating organizations and the LMC, while aggregated insights will help guide future AI-related education, programming, partnerships and support resources for members.

The AI Accelerator is part of a broader effort by LMC and Digital On-Demand Services (DODS), which helps local media organizations get important work done by connecting them with the right experts and managing the work from idea to execution. The AI Readiness & Digital Tech Stack Assessment is supported through funding from the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation as part of the News Media Help Desk, an online resource created by the LMC and The Reynolds Journalism Institute that guides newsrooms toward strategic decisions that ensure the long-term future of local media.

"By helping organizations move from AI experimentation to implementation, this initiative will provide the LMC with valuable insights into the needs and priorities of its membership," said Liz Hayes, program manager for DODS. "Those insights will inform future training programs, educational resources, strategic partnerships and services designed to support local media organizations as they navigate a rapidly evolving technology landscape."

About the Local Media Consortium

The Local Media Consortium delivers more than $60 million in annual economic value through digital partnerships and strategic initiatives on behalf of more than 150 local media companies in top markets across the United States, Canada and Puerto Rico, and includes more than 5,000 newspaper, radio, TV and online-only news outlets. By harnessing the combined volume and scale of its members, the LMC reduces costs and increases revenue with technology and service providers. The aggregated LMC audience footprint spans 200 million unique monthly visitors, and its member companies serve more than nine billion pageviews to consumers. More information is available at localmediaconsortium.com.

releases.title: New Malwarebytes Research Shows Scammers are Tailoring Attacks to Specific Platforms, From Text Toll Scams to Social Media Romance Cons
releases.body:
MrBeast is the most impersonated person, Google is the most impersonated brand, and noon ET on Fridays is the prime time for scam texts

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Malwarebytes, a global leader in real-time cyber protection, released new research showing how criminals are tailoring specific scam types to the platforms where they are most likely to succeed. Nine in ten toll scams, the fake unpaid-toll messages that threaten fines or license suspension, arrive by email or text, while roughly six in ten romance scams play out on social media.

The findings draw on global data from Malwarebytes threat research systems. Malwarebytes analyzed more than 20 distinct scam types, from tech support and refund scams to sextortion and scareware, and found that each one favors a specific delivery channel.

Read the full report

"Scammers are getting more deliberate about where and when they reach people," said Shahak Shalev, Global Head of Scam and AI Research, Malwarebytes. "Certain scams work better on certain platforms, at certain moments, and scammers repeat what works. Knowing where and when particular scams are most likely to appear can help people recognize them before they engage."

Key findings

  • Every scam type has a preferred platform. Fake giveaway scams are far more likely to arrive through a social media feed than by email or text. Half of all IRS scams come by phone call. Job scams favor email, while romance scams mostly arrive through social media, and tech support scams mostly favor phone calls.
  • The web is still the biggest hunting ground. Despite the rise of social media and messaging apps, scams are reaching us through the web more than any other platform, followed by email and SMS.
  • MrBeast is the most impersonated person, ahead of Elon Musk and Donald Trump. MrBeast appears in roughly 30% of impersonation scams tracked by Malwarebytes, ranging from crypto giveaways to transfer-fee swindles. Elon Musk ranks second and Donald Trump ranks third.
  • Noon ET is the "golden hour" for scam texts. Malwarebytes data shows scam text volume peaks at 12 p.m. ET, roughly 874% busier than the quietest hour, 1 a.m. ET.
  • Scam texts build all week and peak on Fridays. Volume rises steadily from a low point on Sunday, and by Friday, people receive roughly 50% more fraudulent text messages than they did at the start of the week.
  • Scammers favor the world's best-known brands. Based on reports from Malwarebytes users, Google, Microsoft, Apple, Roblox, and Amazon are the five most impersonated brands, in that order. Google's name appears in scam content at least twice as often as Amazon's name.
  • Gaming platforms are an increasingly popular target. Roblox, Steam, Discord, and Minecraft were the most impersonated gaming platforms. Roblox saw a 15% spike in scam activity from mid-June to mid-July, and Steam saw a 19% spike over the same period.
  • One in five flagged sessions is high-risk. Malwarebytes Scam Guard, which checks messages, phone numbers, texts, social media messages and links against its threat intelligence database, flags approximately one in five analyzed sessions as high-risk, meaning they could lead to a loss of at least $1,000 or other personal harm.

How to spot and stop scams

Malwarebytes recommends the following steps to reduce risk:

  • Do not click links or call phone numbers in unsolicited emails, texts, or social media DMs.
  • When in doubt, verify a message's legitimacy by going directly to the company's official website and contacting it through official channels. Do not follow sponsored search results to get there, since these can be scams.
  • Never share personal details, PINs, passwords, payment information, or verification codes during an unsolicited call. Legitimate companies will not ask for passwords or verification codes over the phone. Hang up and call back using the organization's official phone number.
  • Use a browser extension that blocks scam and phishing sites, such as Malwarebytes Browser Guard, which can flag a fake storefront before a user lands on it.
  • Install a mobile security product that filters out scam and spam text messages like Malwarebytes Mobile Security alongside comprehensive security with real-time protection for your desktop.
  • Check whether a message is legitimate with Malwarebytes Scam Guard, which analyzes any content, message, phone number, text or link against its threat intelligence database and provides information on red flags and recommended next steps.

Methodology

The data in this report comes from Malwarebytes proprietary threat research systems, collected between April 15 and July 14, 2026. All data is anonymized and reflects what Malwarebytes is able to observe through its own infrastructure.

To read more about the latest threats and cyber protection strategies, visit the Malwarebytes blog, or follow us on Bluesky, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Reddit, and X.

About Malwarebytes

Malwarebytes is reimagining security to safeguard devices, data, and people, no matter their location, lifestyle, or means. A global leader in online protection, its suite of award-winning cybersecurity, privacy, and identity solutions empower millions of people worldwide to enjoy their digital lives, free from threats and scams. Built and beloved by experts, Malwarebytes pairs a world-class team of threat researchers with proprietary AI-powered processes to supercharge and refine detections, providing unmatched protection against both known and unknown threats. Living up to its legacy, Malwarebytes continues to offer free tools that have long served as a first line of defense against malware and scams with new options for identity protection and data removal.

Malwarebytes, powerful digital protection that's always by your side.

Learn more: https://www.malwarebytes.com.

CHICAGO, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GigaStar, the startup bringing Creators and Investors together, announced the launch of GigaStar Securities LLC dba GigaStar Trading, its affiliate broker-dealer platform with a digital Alternative Trading System (ATS) designed to support secondary market trading of Creator Economy digital securities initially purchased on GigaStar Market, its primary investment platform.
releases.title: GigaStar Debuts Its Investing and Trading Ecosystem for the Creator Economy, Rings NASDAQ Bell
releases.body:
GigaStar provides a marketplace for securitized Creator revenue, where investors can buy and now trade these securities through GigaStar Trading, one of the few U.S. platforms operating an SEC-registered digital asset securities ATS.

CHICAGO, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GigaStar, the startup bringing Creators and Investors together, announced the launch of GigaStar Securities LLC dba GigaStar Trading, its affiliate broker-dealer platform with a digital Alternative Trading System (ATS) designed to support secondary market trading of Creator Economy digital securities initially purchased on GigaStar Market, its primary investment platform.

The launch of GigaStar Trading coincides with GigaStar team members ringing the opening NASDAQ Bell in New York City on August 31st, in recognition of the company's 2025 Chicago Innovation Award win.

Previously, Investors could only purchase Creator securities through GigaStar Market, the company's SEC-registered crowdfunding portal, via Regulation CF offerings. With the launch of GigaStar Trading, Investors now have expanded access to buy or sell Creator securities on a regulated secondary market.

While two distinct platforms, GigaStar Market and GigaStar Trading form a connected ecosystem where Investors can access, manage, and trade digital securities representing rights to a percentage of potential future Creator revenue, starting with YouTube revenue.

"We're fueling an asset class that empowers individuals and institutions to participate in the growth of Creators," said David Hunt, CEO of GigaStar Securities. "With the launch of GigaStar Trading, we are introducing broader access to the Creator Economy through an evolving investing and trading ecosystem."

The launch follows GigaStar Securities LLC obtaining registration from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) to operate as a Broker-Dealer and ATS for digital asset securities. GigaStar Trading is one of the few SEC-registered digital asset security ATSs in the U.S., licensed to operate in all 50 states, and, to our knowledge, is the only ATS purpose-built for the Creator Economy.*

  • To date, GigaStar Market has registered 30,000+ Investor accounts and has distributed $1.5M+ in monthly YouTube revenue to Investors.1
  • Since late July, GigaStar Trading has gained 1,000+ accounts, and has cleared $100K+ in trading volume.

Visit GigaStar Trading at gigastartrading.io.

releases.title: Comcast Technology Solutions Unveils Next-Gen Video AI Applications for Broadcasters, Content and Streaming Providers, and Operators
releases.body:
• Building on CTS' VideoAI™ platform, new suite of end-to-end AI-powered workflow applications brings premium content processing capabilities to manage and monetize entire content libraries



  • Applications include video verticalization, localization, smart chapters, metadata enrichment, quality control, and intelligent clip generation



  • Designed to work across CTS' portfolio, including Comcast Media360™, Comcast Sports360™, and standalone Cloud Video Platform deployments

DENVER, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In advance of the 2026 IBC Show, Comcast Technology Solutions (CTS) today unveiled a comprehensive suite of end-to-end AI-powered workflow applications for broadcasters, content owners, and operators worldwide. Building on the foundation of CTS' VideoAI™ platform, these new applications deliver AI as practical, integrated solutions to real-world content production and management challenges.

In a market increasingly crowded with standalone AI vendors and start-ups, CTS aims to serve as a single, trusted partner for end-to-end AI-enhanced content processing, video management, and monetization — backed by the proven reliability and scale of Comcast Technology Solutions and 24/7 managed services. CTS provides end-to-end, production-ready workflow integration that embeds AI capabilities into complete, deployable applications — requiring no additional specialist AI knowledge or developer requirements. The new applications are designed to work across CTS' full product portfolio, including Comcast Media360™ for broadcasters and content owners, Comcast Sports360™ for sports rights holders, and standalone deployments of CTS' Cloud Video Platform (CVP) for operators.

"The video industry is ready to move past AI hypotheticals and onto production-ready applications that solve real problems, generate new business opportunities, and integrate seamlessly into the workflows they already rely upon," said Bart Spriester, Senior Vice President and General Manager of Streaming, Broadcast, and Advertising at Comcast Technology Solutions. "Whether for creating vertical videos, localization, advanced advertising, metadata enrichment, quality control, or intelligent clip generation, CTS stands ready to help our customers benefit from AI to better manage and monetize their content catalogs. CTS VideoAI is based on implementations deployed by some of the world's largest media companies, and we're excited to roll out this package of new applications designed to help our customers of all sizes benefit from that experience in new ways."

Next-Gen AI Applications 

The next-gen AI applications from CTS include:

  • Video Verticalization: Using AI-driven smart cropping technology, CTS can automatically convert landscape video content into portrait format for social media syndication, intelligently identifying the "action center" of each scene and making intelligent cut or pan decisions without manual editor intervention. 
  • Localization of Regional Languages: Leveraging AI-generated voices, CTS can automate dubbing workflows that previously required costly and time-consuming human voice talent. The application can extract audio from soundtracks, preserve ambience and music, translate dialogue, select appropriate voice matching, relay the finished audio back into the content, and generate automated captions. 
  • Smart Chapters: For distribution-ready workflows combining content and ad insertion, CTS can create AI-driven detection of intros, credit rolls, and ad break candidates, enhanced with weighting algorithms to select the optimal set of ad break points and automatically trigger stream conditioning, transcoding, and packaging. 
  • Metadata Enrichment: CTS will automatically generate scene and asset-level metadata and pass it into Cloud Video Platform metadata files, enabling semantic and natural language search capabilities. Rather than traditional keyword searches, content owners will be able to unlock intent-based discovery, allowing customers to find content based on themes, moods, and contextual queries. 
  • Automated Quality Control: CTS will also offer AI-powered "virtual eyes-on-glass" QC checks — including black screen detection, missing audio identification, and other content integrity verifications. This capability can enable cost-effective QC across a significantly larger portion of the content catalog compared to traditional human monitoring approaches. 
  • Intelligent Clipping: CTS will also offer natural language query-driven clip identification and selection, allowing editors to find key moments within long-form content. This could include sports highlights, social media clips, or trailer generation, and then trigger automated processing and publishing workflows.

CTS' new applications are integrated into CTS' Cloud Media Processing (CMP) engine, a flexible, programmable workflow orchestration layer. Processors can be inserted as pre-processors, content manipulation steps, or post-processors, enabling customers to activate individual AI capabilities within their existing workflows without rebuilding their technology stack. For broadcasters and content owners using Comcast Media360, the AI-enhanced workflow processors integrate with existing channel origination and content supply chain services. For sports organizations leveraging Comcast Sports360, capabilities such as intelligent clipping and metadata enrichment are directly applicable to live and on-demand sports content workflows. For MVPDs and operators, these applications will be made available through CTS' Cloud Video Platform. Each of these applications is expected to be made commercially available throughout 2026-2027 to support customer deployments.

Comcast Technology Solutions at IBC 2026

At the 2026 IBC Show, CTS will showcase its next-gen video AI capabilities and full suite of solutions for streaming, broadcast, entertainment, and sports at RAI Amsterdam, September 11–14 in Hall 5, Stand 5.C80. Experts will be on hand to demonstrate the new AI applications and discuss how they integrate across the Comcast Media360, Comcast Sports360, and Cloud Video Platform portfolios. Customers, prospects, and partners of CTS seeking to schedule on-site business meetings can visit: https://www.comcasttechnologysolutions.com/events.

To learn more about Comcast Technology Solutions' entire product portfolio, visit: https://www.comcasttechnologysolutions.com.

About Comcast Technology Solutions

Comcast Technology Solutions, a division of one of the world's leading media and technology companies, brings Comcast Corporation's proven technologies to an evolving list of industries worldwide. Comcast Technology Solutions offers a broad portfolio of solutions that deliver flexibility at scale for global video, media, communications, data applications, and cybersecurity & compliance. Customers include leading content and streaming video providers, pay TV operators and MVPDs, advertisers, communications providers, financial service providers, retailers, and more. For more information, visit Comcast Technology Solutions.

NEW YORK, Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Emplifi, the only Autonomous CX platform, today released findings from its Q2 2026 Social Ads Benchmark Report, revealing strong year-over-year growth in paid social investment spanning regions and industries across Meta ad accounts.
releases.title: Ecommerce social media ad spend surged 70% as brands got more for every dollar
releases.body:
Emplifi analysis of more than 7,700 ad accounts finds ecommerce advertisers increased paid social investment sharply in Q2, while click-through rates rose and cost per click declined.

NEW YORK, Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Emplifi, the only Autonomous CX platform, today released findings from its Q2 2026 Social Ads Benchmark Report, revealing strong year-over-year growth in paid social investment spanning regions and industries across Meta ad accounts.

Based on anonymized data from more than 7,700 Meta ad accounts, the report found that median monthly social ad spend increased 13% year over year across all benchmarks. Ecommerce led industry growth, with median monthly spend rising 70%, from $16,426 in Q2 2025 to $27,966 in Q2 2026.

The increase was accompanied by stronger performance. Ecommerce click-through rates rose 29%, while cost per click declined 18% to $0.133, the lowest of any industry tracked. Across the worldwide benchmark, click-through rates increased 18% year over year, and cost per click declined 9%.

"The brands seeing the biggest efficiency gains on paid social aren't just increasing budgets; they're investing in what happens after the click," said Susan Ganeshan, Chief Marketing Officer at Emplifi. " When the ad lands on relevant content, real customer reviews, and a seamless purchase experience, performance improves. That's what this data is showing us: spend and efficiency moving in the same direction across the full customer journey.

North America sees significant spend growth

North America recorded one of the largest regional increases, with median monthly social ad spend rising 61% year over year, from $8,277 to $13,308.

In the United States, median monthly spend increased 57% to $15,111. Click-through rate rose 22% to 1.78%, the highest of any region tracked, while cost per click declined 3% to $0.483.

The United Kingdom also posted strong growth, with median monthly spend increasing 54%, from $5,257 to $8,074. Click-through rate rose 20%, while cost per click declined 9%.

Europe delivers the strongest efficiency gains

Across Europe, median monthly social ad spend increased 14% year over year to $7,037. Cost per click declined 16%, the largest decrease of any region analyzed, while click-through rate rose 20%.

The data shows that advertisers across the region increased investment while improving both engagement and cost efficiency.

Direct-to-consumer brands, fashion and automotive stand out by industry

Direct-to-consumer brands posted the strongest spend growth of any industry analyzed. Fashion also saw substantial increases, with median monthly spend rising 37% year over year to $18,787. Click-through rate increased 13%, while cost per click declined 17%.

Retail spend increased 14%, accompanied by an 11% increase in click-through rate and a 7% decline in cost per click.

Automotive saw a 24% CTR increase, the strongest engagement gain of any industry in the report, pointing to growing consumer appetite for social as a vehicle research and consideration channel, even as overall spend growth remained modest at 9%.

A full breakdown of the findings is available in Emplifi's analysis, Social Media Ads Benchmarks 2026: Where Paid Social Investment Is Actually Paying Off.

Methodology

Emplifi's Q2 2026 Social Ads Benchmark Report analyzes anonymized data from more than 7,700 Meta ad accounts, spanning global regions and industry verticals. Figures represent median monthly spend, click-through rate, and cost per click per account. Year-over-year comparisons reflect Q2 2026, from April through June 2026, against Q2 2025. Benchmarks are segmented by region, country, and industry, and sample sizes vary by segment.

About Emplifi

Emplifi is the only Autonomous CX platform unifying AI-powered social media management, commerce, and customer care for more than 20,000 brands worldwide. Powered by Fuel AI, built on more than 5T of data, and recognized as a leader by leading industry analysts, Emplifi helps enterprise teams orchestrate connected customer journeys and deliver personalized experiences at scale, turning every customer touchpoint into a competitive advantage.

releases.body:
Continued demand for aggregation across traditional and streaming video drives new bundles and channel combinations

PLANO, Texas, Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Parks Associates' latest consumer research The New Live TV Model: Skinny Bundles, Sports, News finds 27% of US internet households prefer a live-TV bundle combined with their favorite streaming on-demand services, while 24% prefer a skinny bundle combined with their favorite streaming services. In total, 51% prefer a package that combines live TV with their favorite streaming services.

"Consumers are not necessarily choosing between live TV and streaming. Many want access to both in one package," said Michael Goodman, Director, Entertainment Research, Parks Associates. "Providers have the opportunity to offer greater flexibility to their consumers while making it easier to access the content they value."

Parks Associates also finds 68% of streaming pay-TV subscribers (vMVPD subscribers), including consumers using services such as YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo, and DIRECTV Stream, find the idea of a skinny bundle appealing. A skinny bundle is a pay-TV or streaming channel package that includes a limited number of core channels, typically focused on specific content types (e.g., entertainment, sports, or news). It is priced below traditional all-inclusive TV packages.

The findings show consumers continue to value live television, but their expectations for how it is packaged are changing. Smaller channel packages combined with streaming services can provide a middle ground between traditional pay TV and streaming-only options.

"Skinny bundles offer providers an opportunity to address consumers who want to maintain access to live television but are increasingly sensitive to the cost and size of traditional channel packages," Goodman said. "The strongest opportunity is retention. These packages can give existing subscribers another option before they decide to cancel service entirely."

Parks Associates will host the webinar Streaming Video: Churn, Loyalty, and Competition on September 24, featuring research from this study and the Streaming Video Tracker, an ongoing service tracking 400+ streaming video services in North America. The firm is also hosting its ninth annual Future of Video: Business of Streaming on November 17-18 in Marina del Rey, California.

• New Direct-to-Consumer Streaming Service: New streaming service from Cricket Australia (tv.cricket.com.au), built upon Eluvio's Content Fabric and AI Video Intelligence, is now available for early access with full commercial launch later this year



  • Unified Platform for Live and VOD Streaming: Fans can watch ultra-quality live and VOD matches, recent highlights and replays, original documentaries, and archival content enabled by new hyper-efficient Fabric platform



  • Extends use of Eluvio AI in Archive: Cricket TV builds on Cricket Australia's use of Eluvio's frame-accurate AI services to ingest, process, and compose from its deep match archive  

BERKELEY, Calif., Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ahead of IBC Show 2026, Eluvio today announced that Cricket Australia has launched Cricket TV, a new direct-to-consumer streaming service built upon Eluvio's Content Fabric and AI Video Intelligence, extending Cricket Australia's live and archival programming to fans beyond its existing broadcast markets across the globe. Cricket TV is now available for early access with full commercial launch of the service expected later this year at https://tv.cricket.com.au.

"We're excited to extend our partnership with Eluvio as we continue to grow Cricket TV and make Australian cricket more accessible to fans around the world," said Dan Allan, Senior Content Manager, Broadcast at Cricket Australia. "Cricket TV brings live matches and some of the best moments from our archive together in one place for fans around the world. Eluvio has been a fantastic partner throughout the process, helping us deliver a high-quality viewing experience while giving us the flexibility to keep evolving the platform. During the early access period, Cricket TV has already reached viewers in more than 40 countries, highlighting the strong global interest in Australian cricket."

"We're honored to have extended our relationship with Cricket Australia, not only to serve their fans with live matches, but also to serve as a model for other sports organizations looking for the most efficient and cost-effective way to deliver protected sports content with the quality today's global viewers deserve," said Michelle Munson, CEO and Co-founder, Eluvio. "With one Fabric, sports rights holders can unlock dark markets and monetize live and VOD and leverage frame-accurate inline AI, without file copies— all at a fraction of legacy costs while retaining full control of their customers' experience and viewer analytics."

A Unified Platform for Streaming and AI Video Intelligence

Cricket TV provides a white-label browser, mobile, and connected TV application to its viewers built using the Eluvio Media Wallet platform (full turnkey OTT Suite). Cricket TV relies on Eluvio's Content Fabric to receive live matches or archival source feeds and dynamically ingests, transcodes, publishes and generates just-in-time streaming output directly to viewers. Streaming is provided at full source resolution, including HD and 4K, with dynamic automatic adaptation to the user's available bandwidth with low latency HLS/DASH delivery, unlimited multi-view, "zero-copy" live-to-VoD and fast DVR playback. The platform also provides subscriptions, pay-per-view, and/or ad-supported monetization, while providing end-to-end content security and anti-piracy protection including strong encryption, DRM, forensic watermarking, and dynamic authorization per-offering including geo blocking and rights control. All features are built-in allowing for a hyper-efficient, tamper-proof distribution, fast and easy purchasing, and on-screen authenticity proofs for the viewer.

In addition, the Eluvio Video Intelligence Editor (EVIE) and AI-assisted tools provide frame-accurate, in-line analysis, indexing, and search, composition, and transformation such as live vertical video, all without file copies or re-transcoding. Finally, Eluvio Content Analytics provides complete transparency of source-to-viewer audience, QoS, and sales analytics. Full details about Eluvio's technical capabilities and benefits can be found at https://eluv.io

Eluvio at IBC Show 2026

During IBC Show 2026 at the RAI Amsterdam, Eluvio will highlight its work with Cricket Australia and showcase the full capabilities of the Content Fabric and Eluvio AI in Hall 8, Stand 8.MS5, and in the Future Tech Zone, Hall 14, Stand 14.A58, September 11–14, 2026. Eluvio's CEO and co-founder, Michelle Munson, will also speak on the Future Tech Zone stage on Sunday, September 13 from 2:00–2:15 p.m. Registration for one-on-one meetings and information about Eluvio's on-site keynote demonstrations at IBC is available at https://ibc.eluv.io.

About Eluvio

Eluvio (https://eluv.io) is solving the generational problems of video over the Internet with its Content Fabric Protocol — transforming the distribution and monetization of premium video and digital media in contrast to legacy cloud workflows and CDNs. Eluvio serves Amazon Studios/MGM, Cricket Australia, European Professional Club Rugby, FOX, SONY, Telstra Broadcast Services, UEFA, United Rugby Championship, Warner Bros., WPALiveTV, WWE, and others. Led by Michelle Munson and Serban Simu, founders and inventors of Aspera, and based in Berkeley, California. Eluvio holds  more than 15 issued US patents and has won multiple NAB Streaming Product of the Year awards, the Seicon Grand Prize, the Hollywood Professional Association Engineering Excellence Award, and other industry honors. Cricket Australia is the national governing body for the sport of cricket in Australia, responsible for the game at the international, domestic, and grassroots levels, including the Australian Men's and Women's national teams and domestic competitions such as the Sheffield Shield, the WNCL, and the KFC BBL and WBBL. releases.title: UP Argues the Social Media Industry Is Moving From Optional Safeguards Toward Safety by Design
releases.body:
WICHITA, Kan., Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Meta's agreement to pay up to $18 billion in aggregate settlements and make significant changes to Facebook and Instagram marks more than a legal turning point. According to UP, Inc., it marks the arrival of a new market category: Safe Social.

The settlement requires Meta to limit users under 18 to two hours per day across Facebook and Instagram, restrict overnight access, reduce notifications during school hours, strengthen age assurance and parental controls, limit visible "likes" and certain filters, and offer young users a non-algorithmic feed option. Several protections can become stricter if other major platforms adopt comparable terms.

The agreement came during Instagram President Adam Mosseri's testimony and before Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg was expected to testify. Meta denied wrongdoing.

"This settlement validates what families have said for years: social media should not be designed to keep people scrolling at any cost," said Nick Rotola, founder and CEO of UP, Inc. "UP began with a more fundamental question: what if safety was not a setting, but the structure of the product?"

Meta has called on TikTok and YouTube to adopt the same framework. UP believes that pressure confirms that safer defaults are becoming an industry expectation, not a discretionary feature.

But UP argues that guardrails added to an engagement-centered platform are not the same as building a platform around safety from the beginning.

UP screens creators and brands before they can publish. Its standards exclude explicit, violent, hateful, substance-promoting, predatory, and manipulative material. UP does not allow unsolicited direct messages or open comments. Its Scroll Happy® system ranks video around how it may leave a viewer feeling, while mood-based feeds provide greater control.

"Meta is being required to add guardrails around an open, engagement-driven network," Rotola said. "UP vets who can publish, curates what enters the feed, removes unsolicited direct messages, and ranks content for how it leaves a person feeling. That is the difference between safety controls and safety by design."

The risk extends beyond screen time. A 2025 Thorn study found that one in five teens surveyed had experienced sextortion. TIME has also reported allegations concerning Meta's former enforcement thresholds and recommendations connecting potentially inappropriate adults with teens. Meta disputed those allegations.

"The press is calling this social media's tobacco moment. I see it as a millstone moment: a reckoning with what happens when products built to capture attention are allowed to shape children before they are ready to defend themselves," Rotola said. "The settlement matters. But a safer version of the same incentive system is not enough. Families deserve a real alternative."

UP calls that alternative Social with Standards.

UP is available as a free download for iPhone and Android. To learn more, visit www.ScrollHappy.com or download UP through the Apple App Store and Google Play.

About UP, Inc.

UP, Inc. is the company behind UP - Scroll Happy®, a social video platform built around vetted creators, curated content, safer interaction, and user well-being. UP gives people an alternative to doomscrolling through Social with Standards.

releases.title: Gen Z Trusts AI Companies, Influencers and Social Media Least Among 14 Types of Organizations Tested, New Rival Technologies Study Shows
releases.body:
Social media is Gen Z's top source for news, yet just 33% trust social media platforms, while trust in influencers stands at 31% and AI companies at 24%

VANCOUVER, BC, Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AI companies, influencers and social media platforms ranked lowest for trust among 14 types of organizations tested in a new Rival Technologies study of 903 Gen Z consumers across the United States and Canada.

AI companies ranked lowest, with just 24% of respondents expressing trust and 73% expressing distrust, followed by influencers at 31% trust and social media platforms at 33%. The findings are particularly notable given how much Gen Z relies on these platforms and technologies in daily life. Social media, for example, is this generation's top news source, used by 62% of respondents.

Healthcare institutions stood apart, with 79% of Gen Z expressing trust and 31% saying they trust them completely. Trust in most of the other types of organizations tested, including banks, government, traditional news media, food brands and streaming services, fell between the high levels reported for healthcare institutions and the low levels reported for AI companies, influencers and social media platforms.

Top three organizations trusted by Gen Z:

  • Healthcare institutions and hospitals — 79%
  • Hospitality companies (hotels, Airbnb) — 65%
  • Government institutions — 64%

Organizations least trusted by Gen Z:

  • Social media platforms — 33%
  • Influencers — 31%
  • AI tech companies — 24%

Other findings from the study include:

  • Canada is a tougher trust market than the United States. Canadian Gen Zers trust AI companies at less than half the American rate (14% versus 33%), and are far more skeptical of influencers (20% versus 40%) and social platforms (23% versus 43%).
  • Legacy news still holds up. Despite getting most of their news from social feeds, 61% of Gen Z trust established news organizations like The New York Times or The Boston Globe (in the U.S.) or The Globe & Mail (in Canada), nearly double the trust they place in the social platforms carrying that news (33%).
  • Low trust in these categories was consistent across age groups and countries. AI companies, influencers and social media platforms ranked at the bottom across every age group tested and in both the United States and Canada.

"Our research shows that Gen Z trust is fragile, nuanced, and rarely given by default," said Paula Catoira, chief marketing officer at Rival Group."You don't win it with reach, you earn it through relationship. That means meeting these young consumers where they are, and in research, a mobile-first, conversational approach lets them share what they really think in a way that feels natural to them."

The study was conducted with 903 Gen Z participants (ages 18 to 29) across the United States and Canada using Rival's AI-accelerated, mobile-first, conversational research platform, with participants sourced from the company's proprietary panel. It was fielded from late July to early August 2026.

Several solutions from Rival help brands track Gen Z sentiment and attitudes over time.  Emerging Consumer Index tracks Gen Z and millennial consumers across the U.S. and Canada through a continuous research stream, with new data collected every two weeks. Rival Insight Communities give brands access to real-time insights from their most important audiences, including Gen Z.

releases.title: Nashville Predators and ViewLift to Launch New Direct-To-Consumer Streaming Service Ahead of the NHL Season
releases.body:
Multi-Year Agreement Will Bring Fans a Team-Owned Streaming Platform Alongside New Broadcast Deal with Scripps Sports

NASHVILLE, Tenn. and NEW YORK, Aug. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Nashville Predators and ViewLift today announced a multi-year agreement to launch a new direct-to-consumer streaming service for the team, giving fans across Tennessee and beyond access to every locally-carried Predators game starting with the 2026-27 NHL season. The agreement comes after global sports entertainment platform DAZN completed its acquisition of ViewLift last week, and added the Predators to a growing roster of teams and networks, bringing ViewLift's total footprint to 18 U.S. professional sports teams and six Regional Sports Networks nationwide.

The new streaming service will be available across Web, iOS, Android, Apple TV, Roku TV, Fire TV, and Android TV.

The new streaming app will give fans direct access to live games, on-demand replays and highlights, and original programming, all in one place. It will be available on Web, iOS, Android, Apple TV, Roku TV, Fire TV, and Android TV, with additional platforms to be announced. Pricing and trial details will be shared closer to launch.

"This new streaming service will give our fans a direct connection to the team, on their terms," said Bill Wickett, EVP and CMO of the Nashville Predators. "Smashville is one of the most passionate fan bases in the league, and they deserve the flexibility to watch anytime, anywhere, on whatever device they use most. This is just one more way we're investing in how we connect with our fans."

"Nashville is a hockey town with one of the most engaged fan bases in the league, and this alliance reflects that," said Rick Allen, CEO of ViewLift. "We're proud to become the Predators' streaming partner, giving fans in this market full coverage of the team, no matter how they choose to watch. And we're delighted to be working with Scripps Sports on this, our fourth NHL team joint distribution." 

The new streaming service will complement the Predators' broadcast partnership with Scripps Sports, which will air Preds games on "The Spot – Nashville 28" this season. Once launched, the new streaming service will be available across Web, iOS, Android, Apple TV, Roku TV, Fire TV, and Android TV.

About the Nashville Predators

The Nashville Predators were officially welcomed as the NHL's 27th franchise on May 4, 1998, and in the years since have evolved into an integral part of the Middle Tennessee community. Playing in the heart of Broadway and iconic SMASHVILLE at Bridgestone Arena, one of the busiest and most energetic venues in the country, the Predators boast one of the most unique atmospheres in the NHL. The team, which is approaching its 30th anniversary, has qualified for the postseason 16 times, reaching the Stanley Cup Final in 2017, winning the Presidents' Trophy in 2017-18 and capturing two Central Division titles. For more information on the Nashville Predators, including the game schedule and ticket availability, visit NashvillePredators.com.

About ViewLift

ViewLift, a DAZN company, provides digital solutions for content owners, with particular expertise in live and on-demand video distribution. With proprietary cloud-based technology, ViewLift powers digital platforms for sports, media, and entertainment brands worldwide. Its services include content management, multi-platform distribution, real-time analytics, viewer engagement tools, and flexible monetization models (AVOD, SVOD, TVOD, and hybrid models). ViewLift enables content owners to maximize audience engagement and revenue through a seamless, scalable streaming experience. In addition to the Predators, ViewLift's sports clients include the National Hockey League; a total of 18 U.S. professional sports teams; six Regional Sports Networks; the Professional Fighters League; the World Racing Group; and others. The company's media clients include Versant and Kroenke Sports & Entertainment's MOTV.

For more information about ViewLift, visit www.viewlift.com.

releases.title: TELUS unveils new TELUS Wise Digital Content Safety Seal to help parents identify trusted children's programming
releases.body:
The new standard combines the expertise of TELUS Wise, TELUS STORYHIVE and TELUS Digital to recognize programming that meets rigorous safety standards with the TELUS Wise Digital Content Safety Seal

VANCOUVER, B.C., Aug. 18, 2026 /CNW/ -- Today, TELUS introduced the TELUS Wise Digital Content Safety Seal, a new designation provided to Canadian children's programming funded through TELUS STORYHIVE that has successfully completed TELUS' comprehensive digital content safety review. As children spend more time consuming digital content than ever before, the Seal helps families confidently discover Canadian children's programming that meets TELUS' rigorous digital content safety standards. The Seal will debut on eligible children's programming on TELUS STORYHIVE Kids TV, available on TELUS Optik TV Video on Demand channel 611, Stream+ and YouTube.

"Putting families first is at the heart of everything we do at TELUS," says Juggy Sihota, Senior Vice President, Social Impact at TELUS. "By uniting the complementary expertise of TELUS Wise in digital literacy, STORYHIVE in local content creation and TELUS Digital in robust platform moderation, we have built a rigorous framework that protects young media consumers. Programming that meets this elite bar will carry our Safety Seal, giving parents immediate, total confidence in their kids' media choices."

How children's programming earns the TELUS Wise Digital Content Safety Seal

The Seal reflects TELUS' commitment to creating safe experiences for children, both as viewers and as participants in STORYHIVE productions. Developed through a collaboration between TELUS Wise, STORYHIVE and TELUS Digital, the Seal draws on more than a decade of expertise in digital literacy, online safety, Canadian content creation and professional content moderation.

From the earliest stages of development, creators producing children's programming must meet strict requirements, including a mandatory vulnerable sector check for creators working with children, adherence to the STORYHIVE Code of Conduct, child safety protocols and ongoing editorial oversight.

Once completed, programs undergo professional content moderation by TELUS Digital, where they are independently reviewed, classified and assessed against established safety standards. Only programs meeting every requirement earn the right to display the Seal.

What the TELUS Wise Digital Content Safety Seal evaluates



Unlike traditional content ratings that focus primarily on age appropriateness, the Seal recognizes programming that meets rigorous standards for content safety, responsible production practices and educational value. Programming recognized with the Seal reflects a commitment to:

  • Safe, age-appropriate viewing supported by rigorous editorial, production and moderation standards
  • Educational and enriching storytelling that encourages curiosity, creativity and lifelong learning
  • Canadian stories that reflect diverse cultures, perspectives and experiences across British Columbia, Alberta and other Canadian communities
  • Responsible production practices that prioritize child safety throughout content creation

Visit our website to learn more about the TELUS Wise Digital Content Safety Seal and explore TELUS Wise's digital literacy resources.

TELUS is passionate about putting our customers and communities first, leading the way globally in client service excellence and social capitalism. TELUS Digital specializes in digital customer experiences and future-focused digital transformations that deliver value for their global clients.

Since 2000, TELUS and our team members have contributed more than $1.85 billion in cash, in-kind contributions, time and programs to communities across Canada and around the world.

For more information, visit telus.com.

About TELUS Wise

TELUS Wise is a free digital literacy education program which offers workshops and resources covering topics such as protecting your online security, privacy and reputation, rising above cyberbullying and using technology responsibly. Since 2013, TELUS Wise has reached more than 980,000 participants through its educational and informative workshops. Learn more at telus.com/Wise.

TELUS STORYHIVE supports emerging content creators across British Columbia and Alberta through production funding, mentorship, training and national distribution. Since 2013, STORYHIVE has invested more than $74.8 million in Canadian storytelling, empowering creators to share authentic local stories that reflect the communities they call home.
